name: stri_sub<-
title: Replace a substring in a character vector

origin.description: Replace substrings at code-point index ranges and return the new strings.
origin.usage: stri_sub(str, from = 1L, to = -1L, length, omit_na = FALSE, use_matrix = TRUE) <- value

arguments.name: from
arguments.text: Start indexes, or a two-column matrix when use_matrix is TRUE.

arguments.name: to
arguments.text: Inclusive end indexes. Ignored when length is passed.

arguments.name: length
arguments.text: Substring lengths. A negative length leaves that string unchanged. Zero inserts the replacement without deleting.

arguments.name: omit_na
arguments.text: When TRUE, a missing index or a missing replacement leaves that input string unchanged.

arguments.name: use_matrix
arguments.text: When TRUE and from is a matrix, read the two columns as the indexes.

origin.details: The replacement form can inject text at the front, middle, or back when from is past to or past the end. A negative length does not change the string. length wins over to. A missing input string stays missing.
origin.value: The character vector after replacement. In R the replacement operator assigns that vector back to str.
origin.example:
s <- c("spam, spam, bacon, and spam", "eggs and spam")
`stri_sub<-`(s, 1, 4, value = "stringi")

translation.description: Replace substrings at code-point index ranges and return the new strings.
translation.usage: stri_sub_assign(str, from_=1, to=-1, length=None, omit_na=False, use_matrix=True, value)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, or a list of strings. Missing entries are stringi._na.NA.

arguments.name: from_
arguments.text: Start indexes. This is from in R. A list of rows or a dict with two columns is a matrix.

arguments.name: to
arguments.text: Inclusive end indexes. Omitted when length is passed.

arguments.name: length
arguments.text: Substring lengths. A negative length leaves that string unchanged. Zero inserts without deleting.

arguments.name: omit_na
arguments.text: When True, a missing index or a missing replacement leaves that input string unchanged.

arguments.name: use_matrix
arguments.text: True only for a single logical TRUE.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: Replacement strings. This argument is required.

translation.details: This is stri_sub<-. A start past the end appends. If from_ is past to, the replacement is inserted at from_. from_ = 0 and a positive length use from + length - 1 as the inclusive end, which is not the span stri_sub_all_assign uses.
translation.value: A list of the replaced strings.
translation.example:
from stringi.sub import stri_sub_assign
s = ["spam, spam, bacon, and spam", "eggs and spam"]
print(stri_sub_assign(s, 1, 4, value="stringi"))
